# Basic Inferential Data Analysis

We did a descriptive analysis. followed by confidence intervals and hypothesis testing.

## Descriptive Summary
```{r setup, include=TRUE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(summarytools)


data("ToothGrowth")
head(ToothGrowth)
dim(ToothGrowth)
dfSummary(ToothGrowth)
```

- len - Tooth Length - range from 4.2 to 33.9. mean 18.81 and median 19.25.
- supp - Supplement - OJ - Orange Juice - 30 observations and VC - Vitamin C - 30 observations.
- dose - Dose level - 3 doses - 0.5, 1, 2 mg/day for both OJ and VC.

## Overall Supplement Compare

```{r}
t.test(len ~ supp, data = ToothGrowth)
```

Confidence Interval includes 0 [-0.171, 7.571] and p value greater than 0.05. There is no statistically significant difference in tooth growth between groups.

## Supplement at each 3 doses.

```{r}
dose_0.5 <- subset(ToothGrowth, dose == 0.5)
dose_1.0 <- subset(ToothGrowth, dose == 1.0)
dose_2.0 <- subset(ToothGrowth, dose == 2.0)
```

For 0.5 mg/day

```{r}
t.test(len ~ supp, data = dose_0.5)
```

At 0.5mg/day, Orange Juice is more effective than Vitamin C.

For 1 mg/day

```{r}
t.test(len ~ supp, data = dose_1.0)
```


At 1mg/day, Orange Juice is more effective than Vitamin C.


For 2 mg/day

```{r}
t.test(len ~ supp, data = dose_2.0)
```

At 2mg/day, no siginificant difference seen.

## Conclusions and Assumptions

Orange Juice deliver tooth growth over vitamin C except in 2mg dose.
